Read /Users/gabe/Projects/caliper-fixtures/worker-contract.md, then `entire trail finding show 01M7GNVA9XXH --branch feat/scheduler-priority-and-cancel --repo gh/orin-dx/caliper --project gh/orin-dx` and crates/semantic/src/on_demand.rs (`Queue`, `next`, the starvation rule ~lines 160-215). The finding: with a Background request queued, alternating Interactive and Neighbour arrivals can keep the Background request from ever being served (the starvation turn only counts one class or can be reset). Keep it simple: the rule should be that a queued request waits at most N picks (a small constant, say 8) for the higher classes, counted per request or per queue by picks since the oldest lower-class entry was queued, regardless of which higher class is served; after that it gets its turn. A request raised to a higher class keeps the time it was first filed (do not reset its age; this was also a reviewer note: 'a raised request counts as filed when it was raised' is wrong). `Queue::next` also rebuilds the whole deque on each pick (O(n)): replace with a straightforward structure (VecDeque per class + an arrival counter) if it is a small change; skip if it grows the diff. Tests first (fail on base): the exact alternation from the finding (Interactive, Neighbour, Interactive, Neighbour... with one Background queued: Background is served within N picks); raising a request keeps its age; arrival order within a class; cancel still drops queued requests. ONE small property-style test against a reference model (sort by class then arrival, with the starvation rule) is welcome if it is under ~40 lines; otherwise skip. No other changes. Gates (targeted): `just lint doc-check machete typos`, nextest `-p caliper-docgen-semantic` and `-p caliper-docgen-core` (pipeline semantic_hook tests); run `pnpm install --offline --ignore-scripts` in the worktree first if snapshots need @types/react.
